original_question: Does there exist a complete Boolean algebra whose Scott topology is non-sober?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Question 3.7: "Is there a complete Boolean algebra that has a non-sober Scott topology?" ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the correct quantifier (existence), the correct class of structures (complete Boolean algebras), and the correct phenomenon (non-sobriety of the Scott topology). It is essentially the paper’s Question 3.7, rather than the neighboring questions about a specific Boolean algebra of regular open subsets of the reals (Question 3.6) or about complete lattices with enough co-primes (Question 3.5). ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone in the paper’s notation, the object should be written as a complete Boolean algebra B with Scott space ΣB=(B,σ(B)), where σ(B) is the Scott topology on the underlying order of B. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

For complete self-containment, "non-sober" should be understood in the usual topological sense used in the paper: there exists an irreducible Scott-closed subset that is not the closure of a unique point. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The paper does not impose any extra assumptions here such as countability, spatiality, or being a specific Boolean algebra like the regular-open algebra of the reals; those belong to separate nearby questions. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

A slightly more formal phrasing is to say that the Scott space ΣB is non-sober, rather than saying informally that the Scott topology itself is non-sober. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
refined_question: Does there exist a complete Boolean algebra B such that its Scott space ΣB=(B,σ(B)), where σ(B) is the Scott topology on the underlying order of B, is non-sober (that is, some irreducible Scott-closed subset of ΣB is not the closure of a unique point)? ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
justification: The draft is targeting Section 3, Question 3.7 almost verbatim. The surrounding context matters: after recalling earlier non-sober Scott-space examples, the paper states Theorem 3.4 on a spatial frame with non-sober Scott space, then asks in Question 3.5 about complete lattices with enough co-primes, then records Erné’s specific Question 3.6 about the complete Boolean algebra of regular open subsets of the reals, and finally poses the broader Boolean-algebra existence problem as Question 3.7. Hence the closest paper-faithful refinement is exactly Question 3.7, not the narrower regular-open-set problem and not the broader enough-co-primes problem. The only hidden conventions needed for a stand-alone version are the paper’s definitions of Scott space ΣP and sobriety from Section 2. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
